AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: Psoriasis associates several extra-cutaneous manifestations. Little is known about hepatic parameters specifically associated with psoriasis.

AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: To study whether psoriasiform dermatitis is associated with liver injury.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: We studied liver parameters of inflammation and fibrosis in a murine model of psoriasiform dermatitis induced by topical application of imiquimod for nine weeks.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Topical treatment with imiquimod induced a form of psoriasiform dermatitis reminiscent of the human disorder, characterized by thickened and scaly skin, psoriasiform epidermal hyperplasia, altered keratinocyte differentiation, and cutaneous overexpression of interleukin-17A. Mice with dermatitis displayed hepatitis, as shown by elevation of plasma transaminase levels, as well as portal and periportal hepatitis characterized by T lymphocyte (CD3ε+ ) and polymorphonuclear cell (Gr1+ ) infiltrates. The hepatitis progressed toward liver fibrogenesis, as shown by excessive Sirius red staining, consistent with the expression of alpha-smooth muscle actin by hepatic stellate cells.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: These results indicate that liver inflammation and fibrosis is associated with experimental psoriasiform dermatitis. Our results suggest that psoriatic inflammation may be associated with specific liver injury. This article is protected by copyright. All rights reserved.
